new_findings.title: MARKER_TTL_MS (30 s) is a fixed age from ONE write: a live holder whose POST /refresh takes >30 s (slow mobile link, identity DB FOR UPDATE queue) is treated as dead, the stealer POSTs the SAME refresh token at ~30 s -> identity reuse detection revokes the family -> every tab is logged out (G-1 only moved the Y-1 threshold from 10 s to 30 s; the 45 s hard deadline never gets a chance)
new_findings.evidence: (a) holder A: server rotates r1->r2 on arrival, response delayed 35 s; tab B starts 5 ms later. Server log at 29 s: 1 POST; at 31 s: ['refresh(r1) -> ok r2', 'refresh(r1) -> REUSE -> family revoked']. B: AUTH_REQUIRED (401 path clears the session because storage still held r1); A's r2 lands at 35 s into an empty session -> discarded -> A: AUTH_REQUIRED; getSession() === null (buy-flow keys kept by G-4 but useless without a session). (b) holder's request stalls 35 s BEFORE reaching the server: B rotates at 30 s (B:200, storage r2), A's late POST r1 -> REUSE revokes the family incl. r2; A: AUTH_REQUIRED, B keeps a revoked r2 and is logged out at its next refresh (B2: AUTH_REQUIRED, session null). (c) control: holder response at 29 s -> A:200, B:200, 1 POST. Backend: refresh_token_repo.go Rotate() commits r2 BEFORE the response is built (session.go:96-129), so any second POST of r1 is fatal no matter how slow the first one was.
new_findings.fix: Make the marker a heartbeat instead of a one-shot timestamp: while refreshCore's fetch is pending, rewrite {rt, at: Date.now(), id} every ~2-5 s (setInterval cleared in finally); markerFresh() then only expires for a frozen/crashed holder. The stealer keeps waiting while the marker is being refreshed (bounded by HARD_DEADLINE_MS -> NETWORK_ERROR, no POST, no clearSession). Optionally also add an AbortSignal.timeout(~25 s) to the refresh fetch so a live holder gives up before anyone could steal, and treat a timed-out refresh as NETWORK_ERROR (session kept).

new_findings.title: Steal path check-then-write on the marker is not atomic: two tabs that time out in the same instant both steal, the second steal lands before the first stealer wrote its marker, both see 'no marker' and both POST the same refresh token -> family revoked (narrow cross-process window, catastrophic outcome)
new_findings.evidence: Suspended holder (lock held, no marker). Tabs B and C start in the same tick; LOCK_WAIT timers fired with a synchronous vi.advanceTimersByTime(10_000) (no microtask flush between the two timeouts, i.e. two renderer processes reaching the lock manager together). Server log: ['refresh(r1) -> ok r2', 'refresh(r1) -> REUSE -> family revoked']; outcomes ['B:NETWORK_ERROR', 'C:AUTH_REQUIRED'] (B's steal was stolen before it wrote the marker, so B's AbortError catch path finds no marker and throws NETWORK_ERROR; B's background POST stores a revoked r2); B's next refresh -> AUTH_REQUIRED, session null. Control with 5 ms between the two tabs and microtask flushes: 1 POST, B:200, C:200.
new_findings.fix: Inside the steal callback, claim before acting: write the marker {rt, id, at} FIRST (synchronously, before any await), wait one short tick (~50-100 ms), re-read it and proceed only if the id is still ours; otherwise fall into waitForRotation. In the AbortError catch path, wait a short grace period (poll a few times) before concluding 'no marker' so that a thief that is about to write its marker is honoured instead of throwing NETWORK_ERROR immediately.

new_findings.title: Stolen-steal catch path maps 'session gone' to NETWORK_ERROR: when tab B's own steal is stolen by tab C and B's own POST then fails 401 (family already revoked, e.g. logout elsewhere), B's refreshCore clears the session but B's request resolves NETWORK_ERROR ('thử lại') instead of AUTH_REQUIRED ('đăng nhập')
new_findings.evidence: Suspended holder; B steals at 10 s and POSTs (500 ms, 401 unauthorized); C (started 200 ms later) steals at 10.2 s. Result: C: AUTH_REQUIRED, B: NETWORK_ERROR, getSession() === null. The waiting-room / checkout UI shows a retry prompt for B while the session is already wiped; the retry then goes out without a Bearer.
new_findings.fix: In the AbortError catch of the steal path, when waitForRotation returns null because getSession() is null (not because of the deadline), throw AUTH_REQUIRED; also prefer awaiting the tab's own in-flight doRefresh promise (keep a `mine` reference like the normal path does) so its real outcome (401 -> AUTH_REQUIRED, 200 -> token) is surfaced.

new_findings.title: G-4 keeps buy-flow keys on involuntary expiry, but nothing clears them when a DIFFERENT user then signs in on the same tab (loginUser / loginWithGoogle only call setSession): user B inherits user A's ef:queue:token:e1, evenflow_hold_e1 (getActiveHold resumes A's order), ef:pay:*, ef:issue:* (F-17 shared-computer concern re-opened for the expiry path; also true for a plain re-login as another user without any expiry)
new_findings.evidence: seedSession u-1 + buy-flow keys; refresh 401 -> AUTH_REQUIRED, session null, keys kept (G-4 by design). loginUser as u-2 (login 200) -> getSession().user.id === 'u-2' and sessionStorage still holds 'ef:queue:token:e1' = 'x', getActiveHold('e1').orderId === 'o-A', 'ef:pay:o1:h', 'ef:issue:o1'. Same with loginWithGoogle as u-2 and with a direct login as u-2 while u-1 was still signed in. Control: explicit logout() then login -> keys null.
new_findings.repro:
it('B inherits A keys', async () => { seedSession('old','r1'); for (const k of KEYS) sessionStorage.setItem(k,'x'); sessionStorage.setItem('evenflow_hold_e1', JSON.stringify({orderId:'o-A',holdId:'h-A',expiresAt:'2030-01-01T00:00:00Z',ticketTypeId:'t1',quantity:2})); installFetch(c=>{ if(c.path==='/api/v1/auth/refresh') return problem(401,'/problems/unauthorized'); if(c.path==='/api/v1/auth/login') return json({id:'u-2',role:'buyer',access_token:'acc-B',refresh_token:'r-B',expires_in:900}); return problem(401,'/problems/token-expired'); });
 await expect(apiFetch('/v1/orders/o1')).rejects.toMatchObject({code:'AUTH_REQUIRED'}); await loginUser('b@b.co','pw'); expect(getSession()?.user.id).toBe('u-2'); expect(sessionStorage.getItem('ef:queue:token:e1')).toBe('x'); expect(getActiveHold('e1')?.orderId).toBe('o-A'); });
new_findings.fix: Remember the last signed-in user id (e.g. localStorage ef_last_uid written by setSession) and in storeFromIdentity / setSession call clearBuyFlowStorage() when the new session's user.id differs from it; alternatively scope the buy-flow keys by user id (ef:{uid}:queue:token:...).

new_findings.title: G-8 read-only state of a just-created tier depends on setEvent(await reload()) succeeding, not on the swap: when the GET after the failed POST also fails (same network blip), the swapped tier (now carrying the server id srv-new-1) stays name/price-editable and deletable; a rename is silently dropped on retry (Y-11 class), and if the retry's reload fails too the created map (keyed by the LOCAL id) cannot match the server id and the tier is POSTed again -> duplicate tier on the server

Plan [.., FAIL, FAIL]: addTier names ['Hạng vé #2','Hạng vé #3','Hạng vé #2','Hạng vé #3'], third call's tier.id === 'srv-new-1'. Control (reload ok): tier #2 disabled, 1 delete button, no duplicate.

new_findings.fix: Make the wizard derive read-only-ness from the swap itself: keep a `createdIds` state (extended by applyCreatedTiers) and treat `existingTierIds.has(id) || createdIds.has(id)` as existing. In EditForm, key the created map by BOTH the local id and the server id (or look up `created` values by server id) so a tier whose id was swapped is never re-POSTed, and on a failed reload merge `created.current` values into the comparison set instead of using the stale prop.

checked_no_finding: Crashed holder leaving a fresh marker with the lock free: the next tab is granted the lock immediately and POSTs at once (marker ignored on the normal path), 1 POST, marker cleared. Crashed holder's marker + lock held by a suspended tab: the waiter POSTs when the marker is 30 s old (here at ~11 s, marker written 20 s earlier), not at the 45 s deadline.
Marker for r1 while storage already holds rotated r2: waiter with usedRefresh r1 returns r2's access token, 0 POSTs.

Hard deadline (45 s) with the stolen-lock POST still in flight: NETWORK_ERROR, session (r1) and buy-flow keys kept, late r2 is stored and reused by the next request without another POST. Retry at 46 s while the background steal callback still holds the lock: queued behind own callback, 1 POST total.
G-1 marker cleanup: clearMarker only removes its own id, so a stealer's marker is not wiped by the earlier holder's finally.

AUTH_REQUIRED/NETWORK_ERROR outcomes: refresh 401 with storage unchanged -> clearSession + AUTH_REQUIRED (buy-flow keys kept, G-4); storage already rotated by another tab -> AUTH_REQUIRED for that request only, session kept; deadline -> NETWORK_ERROR. Only the Z-3 corner is inconsistent.

Payment key scoping (G-5): identical retry after AMBIGUOUS x3 reuses the key; a changed buyerName (even trailing space; the hook trims) / method / phone / amount / holdId gives a new key; going back to the first body reuses its key. returnUrl is NOT in the hash but IS in the body the server hashes -> a caller that varies returnUrl would get 422 key-reused (INVALID_INPUT); no caller passes returnUrl (use-payment-session), so not a finding. Old body-scoped keys linger in sessionStorage (3 keys after 3 bodies) until logout: harmless.

Y-7 second half (auto rotate on urn:eventflow:problem:idempotency-key-reused) is still not implemented, but with body-scoped keys it is only reachable via a 32-bit FNV collision or the returnUrl case above.

SOLD_OUT quota-only: real updateTierQuota blocks decreases (no PUT) and sends PUT on increase; equal quota valid; ModerationStatusCard and EventList expose the 'Tăng số lượng vé' link for SOLD_OUT; EventWizard header mentions SOLD_OUT.
G-8 happy path (reload succeeds): created tier read-only, quota change of the created tier goes through updateTierQuota(srv-new-1), no re-POST.

One-shot sign-in identifier (G-7): logout()/clearSession/setSession do not touch ef:signin:identifier (not a buy-flow prefix); it is consumed exactly once by LoginForm; the register link href is a bare /auth/sign-in. Residual: if the user never reaches LoginForm the identifier stays in that tab's sessionStorage until the tab closes (own identifier, own tab; not a finding).

clearSession scopes: api-client's three clearSession() calls (no session, refresh 4xx, invalid refresh body) keep buy-flow keys; only logout() passes {buyFlow:true}; use-payment-session / hold-client never call clearSession.
suspicions_no_repro: Remember-me off (sessionStorage sessions) in two tabs = two token families sharing one origin-wide lock and one marker key: a slow refresh in one tab delays the other tab's refresh by LOCK_WAIT_MS (10 s) before it steals; markerFresh(rt) mismatches so no reuse, just latency. Not modelled (jsdom shares sessionStorage between the two module instances).

waitForRotation polls with setTimeout(250 ms) and never listens to `storage` events; in a hidden tab Chrome throttles chained timers to 1 s (intensive throttling: 1 min after 5 min hidden), so both the poll and the 45 s hard deadline stretch; a `storage` listener would wake the waiter immediately.

Backend (out of FE scope): services/identity/internal/app/session.go Refresh() commits Rotate() before FindByID/device registration; a failure after the commit returns 5xx with r1 consumed and r2 never delivered, so the FE's correct 'keep session on 5xx' then ends in REUSE on the next refresh.
